title: Anlo: The People Who Walked Backwards

pages.text: On the first Saturday of November, thousands of people fill the durbar ground at Anloga in the Volta Region. Chiefs arrive under umbrellas. Drummers play agbadza, and the dancers bend and sweep their arms like birds. Then comes a moment that puzzles visitors. A group of people act out a journey, and they walk backwards. This is Hogbetsotso, the festival of the Anlo people. Its name means the festival of leaving Hogbe, their old home. The backward steps tell of one night, about four hundred years ago, when a whole people slipped away from a cruel king.

pages.text: Ewe tradition says that their ancestors travelled west in stages from a town called Ketu, in what is now the Republic of Benin. They settled for a long time at Notsie, in present-day Togo. Notsie was a large town surrounded by a thick wall of earth. At first the people lived there in peace. Then came a king named Agorkoli. The stories say that he was harsh. He gave the people cruel and impossible tasks, such as making rope out of clay. The elders decided, in secret, that it was time to leave.

They settled for a long time at Notsie, in present-day Togo.
Notsie was a large town surrounded by a thick wall of earth.
At first the people lived there in peace.
Then came a king named Agorkoli.
The stories say that he was harsh.
He gave the people cruel and impossible tasks, such as making rope out of clay.
The elders decided, in secret, that it was time to leave.
pages.alt: A large town of round houses enclosed by a high, thick earth wall.

pages.text: The wall was the problem. It was too high to climb and too strong to break, and the gates were guarded. So the women were told to throw all their washing water against one spot on the wall, every day. Slowly, the earth became soft. One night there was loud drumming and dancing to cover any noise. The wall was pushed through, and the people passed out: women and children first, then the elders, then the young men. The last to leave walked backwards, so that their footprints seemed to lead into the town and not away from it.

pages.alt: A line of people slipping at night through a gap in an earth wall, with drummers playing in the background.

pages.text: The groups went different ways, and they became the many Ewe peoples of Ghana and Togo. One group, led by an elder named Wenya and his nephew Sri, travelled south to the coast. They reached a narrow strip of sand between the sea and a great lagoon. Wenya, old and tired, is said to have told them that he had curled up and could go no further. From his words came the name Anlo. Their capital was built at Anloga. Sri became the first king, the Awoamefia, a ruler who was honoured as sacred and lived apart from public view.

pages.alt: A narrow strip of sandy land with palm trees, the sea on one side and a wide lagoon on the other.

pages.text: It was a hard land to live in. The soil was sandy and the sea was rough. The Anlo learned to use what they had. From the Keta Lagoon they collected salt and traded it far inland. They became famous sea fishermen, and their crews still work beaches all along the coast of West Africa. At Anloga, farmers found a way to grow shallots in sand. Weavers at Agbozume made fine cloth. A war leader, the Awadada, commanded the army. Today the sea itself is the enemy at Keta. It has washed away whole streets, and a sea wall now protects the town.

pages.text: Before Hogbetsotso begins, there is a time for making peace. Families and neighbours must settle their quarrels, and the towns are swept clean. Only then can the celebration start. So the festival does three things. It keeps a people’s history alive without a single written page. It reminds leaders that people will leave a ruler who treats them badly. And it teaches that a new beginning needs clean hearts as well as clean streets. Each time the dancers step backwards at Anloga, they are telling their children where they came from, and why.

activities.question: Why did the elders at Notsie decide to leave?
options: King Agorkoli treated the people harshly
They wanted to live nearer the sea

activities.question: How was the wall at Notsie weakened?
options: It was knocked down by elephants
The women threw water on one spot until the earth became soft

activities.question: Why did the last people to leave walk backwards?
options: So that their footprints would seem to lead into the town

activities.question: Apply it: Before Hogbetsotso, people must settle their quarrels. Which school practice is most like this?
options: Solving a disagreement between classmates before starting a group project

activities.prompt: Put the steps of the escape and settlement in order.
items: The Ewe settle inside the walls of Notsie
King Agorkoli gives the people cruel tasks
The women soften the wall with water
The people leave at night, the last walking backwards
Wenya and Sri lead one group to the coast and found Anlo
